title: Quantization anchor + per-head safety-net for model-specific outlier mitigation
creator: Marco Chen
description: Implement a model-specific mitigation that combines an anchored layer-scale correction with a per-head percentile-based safety-net to reduce post-quantization accuracy regressions for LLama, Mistral, and Qwen families. Goal: stop single-head or single-layer outliers from causing large downstream token distribution shifts during FP8/INT8 serving while keeping latency and memory overheads minimal.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model calibration profile that reduces top-1 token-change regression vs float32 by >= 60% on internal eval sets for each model family
No more than 1% additional median latency at p99 compared to current quantized baseline for 512-token inference
Automated calibration pipeline completes for each model in < 45 minutes on a 4-GPU calibration pool
Regression alerting hooks integrated into CI evals and console regression dashboard (test harness PR linked).
technical_approach: Collect layer-wise activation percentiles and head-wise spike histograms from representative calibration corpus per model (LLama/Mistral/Qwen)
Compute an anchor scale per layer: a conservative multiplicative factor derived from 99.9th percentile of activations with a smoothing prior to avoid oscillation between releases
Per-head safety-net: store head-specific percentile thresholds and apply selective soft-clipping at runtime when a head's activation exceeds its threshold
Hybrid FP8/INT8 policy: prefer FP8 for layers with >5% sensitivity in token-distribution drift tests; fallback to INT8 with anchoring for heavy512/long-sequence layers
Calibration outputs: a compact profile (one float per layer anchor + per-head threshold table compressed via run-length encoding) loaded by runtime kernel selection
Runtime changes: small pre-kernel rescale step and branch to safety-net clip path only when percentile breach is detected to minimize overhead
Evaluation harness: run prompt suite of 12k tokens across model variants and compare sampling divergence, log-odds deltas, and perplexity changes
calibration_workflow: Stage 1: Harvest activation distributions using a stratified corpus (docs, dialogue, code) — script: tools/quant/harvest_activations.py
Stage 2: Fit layer anchor by minimizing worst-case KL divergence over calibration corpus with L2 regularizer to float activations
Stage 3: Compute per-head percentile thresholds at 99.5/99.9 for candidate clipping and validate impact on generation via the eval harness
Stage 4: Synthesize final profile into runtime format and run runtime smoke tests on dedicated calibration nodes
Stage 5: Push profile to canary deployment (10% traffic) and monitor quality regressions and token-level deltas
evaluation_plan: Baseline: float32 outputs and current quantized baseline (no anchoring) on evaluation prompt set
Primary metrics: token-level KL, top-1 token flip rate, MRR for reranking prompts, and human-labeled pass/fail for 500 sampled prompts
Stability metrics: distribution of layer anchor adjustments across releases, frequency of safety-net activation per 1k tokens
Performance metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, memory delta, CPU pre-rescale overhead percentage
Alerting thresholds: token flip rate regressions >3% or KL increases >0.12 trigger a rollback
rollout_plan: Internal canary: deploy to dedicated canary pool for each model family (10% of internal traffic) for 72 hours
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 6 days if no regressions
Fallback: automatic switch to model-variant without anchoring if regression threshold exceeded; immediate alert to SRE and Quant team
Post-rollout: capture 7-day telemetry and produce a short RCA if any anomalies observed
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created after initial offline experiments showed single-head spikes cause >7% token flip for Qwen-Base under INT8
2025-02-18: Harvested calibration corpus and ran collection job for LLama-2-13B and Mistral-7B; dataset stored at gs://redwood-quant/calib/2025-02
2025-02-22: Prototype anchor formula (anchored_scale = max(1.0, p999/p95 * 0.9)) reduced worst-case KL by ~40% on LLama-13B but over-clipped some rare-code tokens
2025-02-27: Switched to smoothed anchor with L2 prior; implemented per-head percentile table generator and compression serializer
2025-03-03: Runtime pre-rescale microbenchmarks show +0.6% median latency and +1.1% p99 for 512-token requests; safety-net branch rarely taken in steady traffic
2025-03-04: Started canary profiles for Mistral family; monitoring hooks pushed to console regression dashboard (dashboard link attached).
test_results: LLama-2-13B float32 -> anchored-FP8: top-1 flip reduced from 9.8% to 3.6% on dev prompts
Mistral-7B INT8 + anchor: KL reduction 0.08 -> 0.03 median across domains
Qwen-Base INT8 initial: worst-case token flip 12%; with anchor+safety-net: 4.1%
Calibration runtime per-model: 34 minutes average on 4xA100-80GB pool
notes: We must watch for over-clipping in code-heavy prompts — introduced a per-domain weight during anchor fitting
Compression format for per-head tables chosen to keep profile < 64KB for base models; larger models may require segmented profiles
Follow-up work: explore dynamic online adaptation where anchors slowly update from live telemetry (future ticket)
Design trade-off: We accept small median latency increase to avoid high-tail accuracy regressions which are much harder for downstream apps to handle
